script.base: Books have Denver leading a mid-40s game, not a shootout. Base flow is DEN ahead by a score by the second half, leaning on J.K. Dobbins (46 carries, 149 rush yards over weeks 4-6) against an ARI run defense allowing 4.44 YPC, with Bo Nix not forced into a pass-heavy script. ARI trails with Jacoby Brissett, stays on Trey McBride (31 targets) and Michael Wilson (27), but Denver's 37% blitz (Brissett -0.24 EPA/dropback vs blitz, n=67) stalls drives with negative plays rather than a clean yardage shootout.
script.flip1: DEN jumps up by 14+ early and clocks it: Dobbins carries spike, Jaylen Waddle/Courtland Sutton/RJ Harvey receiving stalls (same shape as a favorite finishing well under his pass props), and ARI abandons the committee run so Tyler Allgeier (29/87) and Zonovan Knight (16/88) rush lines die.
script.flip2: ARI's soft pass defense (8.27-8.84 YPA, 19 passes of 20+ on 188 att) gashes Denver early, DEN chases, Dobbins carries fall, and Waddle plus the ARI primary receivers clear overs together.

injury_fallout: No injury report, practice status, questionable tags, or inactives in the pack, so no named next-man-up from a confirmed scratch. L3 usage is the only role evidence: Dobbins is the carry share (46 of the listed DEN RB carries vs Harvey 16, Badie 5, Nix 9); Harvey is the checkdown (15 targets, -32 air yards); Waddle leads DEN targets (18) over Sutton (12) and Engram (11). ARI backfield is a committee (Allgeier 29, J.Love 26, Knight 16, Brissett 8) with McBride/Wilson the pass volume. Props for Jonah Coleman, Troy Franklin, and Adam Trautman have no L3 production in the pack — role unknown, not treated as injuries. Re-check would be required at the final injury report; that checkpoint is not in this pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Proxy only: ARI allows soft YPA to every field (left 8.84 on 64 att, middle 8.27 on 45, right 8.67 on 63). DEN is tighter outside (left 6.86 on 69, right 5.34 on 100) and soft in the middle (9.1 on 41).
matchup.pressure: ARI blitzes only 28%, so Nix's blitz problem (EPA/dropback -0.27 on 66 blitz dropbacks vs -0.02 unblitzed) is not the base case and does not force a Harvey/Engram checkdown game by itself. DEN blitzes 37% into a Brissett who is -0.24 EPA vs blitz (n=67) and +0.11 unblitzed — pressure is the ARI-offense problem, which cuts explosive conversion more than it creates easy WR overs.
matchup.bleeds: ARI run defense bleeds: 4.44 YPC allowed and 19 runs of 10+ in 6 games, plus a 10.1% explosive-pass rate (19 of 188). DEN run defense also bleeds (4.83 YPC, 24 runs of 10+) but DEN allows only 15 passes of 20+ on 229 att.
matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is Dobbins' bellcow carries into ARI's 4.44 YPC / 19 explosive-run defense in a DEN -4.5 script. Waddle leads DEN targets (18) but at 78 yards (4.3 per target) and only 102 air yards (5.7 aDOT), so he is not the player attacking ARI's explosive-pass bleed — Sutton is (152 air yards on 12 targets, 41 receiving yards). McBride (31 targets, 173 air) overlaps DEN's middle (9.1 YPA), but 150 yards on those targets plus the blitz EPA split argue against forcing over 62.

form: Avoiding season averages. DEN L3: Dobbins 46/149 rush (3.24 YPC, ~15.3 carries/game) and only 7 targets/23 rec yards; Harvey 16/57 rush plus 15 targets/99 rec yards on negative air yards; Waddle 18 targets/78 yards/102 air, well under a 51.5 line; Sutton 12/41/152 air, a deep-shot role that is not converting. ARI L3: McBride 31/150/173 (~50 rec ypg, 4.8 yards/target); Wilson 27/157/310 air (~52.3 ypg, right on 49.5); Allgeier 29/87 rush (3.0 YPC) in a committee; Knight 16/88 (5.5 YPC) but only ~5.3 carries/game; Higgins 8 targets/104 yards on just 31 air yards looks YAC-spike dependent and is not used. No similar-defense game splits beyond these L3 totals vs the season defensive rates above.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Dobbins is the clock-control back for a 4.5-point favorite against a run defense allowing 4.44 a carry and 19 runs of 10+, so a ~15-carry role should clear 48.5 even if efficiency only ticks up from his recent 3.24 YPC.
edge_players.must_be_true: Dobbins active with no snap cap, DEN not chasing by double digits, and carry share staying near the L3 46-carry lead over Harvey/Badie/Nix.
edge_players.kills_it: DEN falls behind and abandons the run, or Harvey (16 L3 carries) and Badie steal the positive-script work and hold Dobbins near 10 carries.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Waddle's Denver role is 6 targets and 26 receiving yards a game at a short 5.7 aDOT, and a Denver lead leans Dobbins, so 51.5 is priced for a WR1 explosive day his usage is not getting — Sutton, not Waddle, is the deep shot into ARI's soft secondary.
edge_players.must_be_true: Waddle stays in the 5-7 target, non-deep role from weeks 4-6, and DEN does not need a pass-heavy chase script.
edge_players.kills_it: Shootout or deficit flip: ARI's 8.3-8.8 YPA and 19 explosive passes let even a modest target bump at normalized efficiency clear 51.5, or a late target spike if Sutton is quiet.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so step 8 cannot price against a sharp book. Pack form agrees with direction: Dobbins 149 rush yards over 3 games = 49.7 ypg vs 48.5, with ARI's 4.44 YPC allowed as the efficiency bump the average alone does not show; Waddle 78 yards on 18 targets = 26 ypg vs 51.5 under. Neither leg is a 70%+ model claim. Sutton under 34.5 and McBride over 62 were not used: Sutton's 152 air yards overlap ARI's explosive bleed (data would fight an under that is only a cold streak), and McBride's 50 ypg vs 62 plus -0.24 blitz EPA is a lean the pack does not support, so those were dropped rather than flagged.

market_rung_price: jkdobbins rushyds over 48.5 -109.5 (near even, not a short alt); jaylenwaddle recyds under 51.5 -114. No no-vig or sim rung in the pack. Same-player rushrecyds alts (Dobbins 58, Harvey 46.5) skipped — one market per player. Several other listed prices are +nan and unused.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because Denver never led: ARI's pass defense, which allows 8.27-8.84 YPA and 19 passes of 20+ on 188 attempts, turned Waddle's 6-target role into one efficient chunk day over 51.5, and once Denver chased, Dobbins was capped near 10 carries and finished under 48.5 at his recent 3.24 YPC. The same miss happens if Harvey's 16 L3 carries or a late inactive (not in this pack) splits the bellcow work even in a Denver lead. The Waddle under is the fragile leg — the counter-case is a bad secondary, not a hidden target share — so it stays a lean, not a strong anchor.
slip_story: One story only: favorite runs the clock. DEN -4.5 leads, Dobbins rush-yards over is the anchor, Waddle receiving-yards under is the correlated pass-volume cap. Do not pair with McBride/Wilson overs, a game total over, or Sutton over — those need the shootout flip. No TDs, no receptions, no passing yards.
